01

Setting specification

Task

Find an approximately stationary primal point of the value function formed by maximizing the average of the component payoffs over the dual variable.

$$ \min_x\Phi(x),\quad\Phi(x)=\max_y\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x,y). $$

Admissible model

Assume $f=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i$, with each $f_i:\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_y}\to\mathbb{R}$ continuously differentiable. For all full-space points $z,w$,

$$ \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|\nabla f_i(z)-\nabla f_i(w)\|_2^2\le\beta^2\|z-w\|_2^2. $$

Only the mean function $f(x,\cdot)$ must be uniformly $\mu_y$-strongly concave. Components need not be concave or individually $\beta$-smooth; $f(\cdot,y)$ and $\Phi$ may be nonconvex.

The public initial point is $(0,0)$, with promises $y^\star(0)=0$ and $\Phi(0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta<\infty$. Attainment of the primal minimum is not required. Assume $n\ge2$ and $\kappa=\beta/\mu_y\ge1$.

Oracle interface

Public inputs include block dimensions $d_x,d_y$ and $\Delta$, $\beta$, $\varepsilon$, $\mu_y$, and $n$, together with the stated initial points and feasible-set information. Analytic representations of hidden functions, operators, and matrices are not supplied.

$$ (i,x,y)\longmapsto\nabla f_i(x,y),\quad i\in\{1,\ldots,n\},\ (x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_y}. $$

The algorithm selects a component index and query point. Each index always refers to the same fixed component. The response is its exact full joint gradient, without a function value, Hessian, best response, or reduced gradient. There is no random oracle noise.

Output

Return a single primal point $\widehat{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$; no dual point or computable certificate is required.

Loss or accuracy criterion

Accuracy is the Euclidean norm of the gradient of the reduced average payoff at the returned primal point. The expected-error views bound its mean square by $\varepsilon^2$. The fixed-probability view requires the norm to be at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $2/3$.

$$ \|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2 $$

$\nabla\Phi(x)=\nabla_x f(x,y^\star(x))$.

Resource accounting

One component joint-gradient call counts once in $N_{\rm component}$. A complete mean gradient requires $n$ calls.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Randomized zero respecting expected rms

Randomized adaptive zero-respecting algorithms are permitted. The first query is at $(0,0)$. At query $t$, the supports of $x$ and $y$ lie in the unions of the corresponding previously returned gradient supports. The support of output $\widehat{x}$ lies in the union of all returned $x$-gradient supports.

Component indices, values on exposed coordinates, and stopping decisions may be fully adaptive. Unexposed coordinates or arbitrary coordinate rotations cannot be used to circumvent the support restriction.

Choose one algorithm, then require the guarantee for every admissible instance and stochastic-feedback mechanism.

$$ \mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2\right)^2\right]\le\varepsilon^2. $$

Expectation is only over the algorithm's private seed. Exact responses from fixed components contain no oracle noise.

Output qualification. Unqueried outputs are allowed but must obey the stated zero-respecting rule.

Resource qualification. Use expected work on the worst instance. The algorithm stops almost surely, with call count $\tau$ satisfying $\sup_I\mathbb{E}[\tau]\le N$. This does not require every execution path to finish within $N$ calls.

Budget convention
worst-case expected total component calls; random stopping allowed

Randomized unrestricted expected rms

Arbitrary measurable sequential adaptive randomized algorithms are allowed. The private seed is independent of the hidden instance. Queries, stopping, and output may use the full history, without additional span, zero-respecting, communication, or memory restrictions.

Choose one algorithm, then require the guarantee for every admissible instance and stochastic-feedback mechanism.

$$ \mathbb{E}\!\left[\left(\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2\right)^2\right]\le\varepsilon^2. $$

Expectation is only over the algorithm's private seed. Exact responses from fixed components contain no oracle noise.

Output qualification. The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.

Resource qualification. Use expected work on the worst instance. The algorithm stops almost surely, with call count $\tau$ satisfying $\sup_I\mathbb{E}[\tau]\le N$. This does not require every execution path to finish within $N$ calls.

Budget convention
worst_instance_expected_calls

Randomized unrestricted fixed probability

Arbitrary measurable sequential adaptive randomized algorithms are allowed. The private seed is independent of the hidden instance. Queries, stopping, and output may use the full history, without additional span, zero-respecting, communication, or memory restrictions.

A single algorithm is chosen from the public input and must satisfy the guarantee for every fixed admissible instance.

$$ \Pr\!\left(\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2\le\varepsilon\right)\ge\frac23. $$

Probability is over private algorithmic randomness only. The unknown instance is fixed before interaction.

Output qualification. The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.

Resource qualification. Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified $N$ on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.

Budget convention
fixed_worst_case_cap

Notation and parameters

$\Delta$

A public bound on the initial reduced-objective value above its infimum. Attainment of the infimum is not required.

Domain
Positive real number

$\Phi(0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta$

$\beta$

Mean-square average Lipschitz upper bound for component joint gradients

Domain
Positive real number

$\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\|\nabla f_i(z)-\nabla f_i(w)\|_2^2\le\beta^2\|z-w\|_2^2$

$c_0$

Universal small constant in the lower-bound accuracy window; no numerical value is specified.

Domain
Positive constant without an assigned numerical value
$d$

The joint Euclidean dimension is $d=d_x+d_y$. Within its stated window, the lower bound may choose finite block dimensions.

Domain
Integer at least $2$
$\varepsilon$

Euclidean norm tolerance for the true reduced gradient; the mean-square contract targets its square $\varepsilon^2$.

Domain
Positive real number
$\kappa$

Ratio of the population smoothness upper bound, or mean-square average smoothness for finite sums, to the dual strong-concavity lower bound

Domain
$\kappa\ge1$

$\kappa=\beta/\mu_y$

$\mu_y$

A uniform strong-convexity lower bound for −f(x,·) at every fixed x; equivalently, the dual strong-concavity modulus of f.

Domain
$0<\mu_y\le\beta$

$f(x,v)\le f(x,y)+\langle\nabla_yf(x,y),v-y\rangle-\frac{\mu_y}{2}\|v-y\|_2^2$

Fixed number of finite-sum components; the full function or operator is their 1/n average

Domain
Integer at least $2$
$\|\cdot\|_2,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$

Euclidean norm and inner product; the product-space norm is the square root of the sum of the squared block norms.

Domain
The specified finite-dimensional real vector space.

$\|v\|_2=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$

B9

Embedding an arbitrary-randomized finite-sum lower bound with an independent strongly concave quadratic term

Dense Weak Hiding: Closing Complexity Gaps in Nonconvex and PL Finite-Sum Optimization under Individual Smoothness ↗
Conditions
Every condition in the eight-axis specification and associated regime must hold jointly. Sufficient constants from different theorems are not assumed identical.
Algorithm scope
A lower bound for arbitrary randomized algorithms.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Constants
Use the source theorem’s universal constants except where derivative order or structural budgets are explicitly fixed. Unspecified sufficient thresholds remain symbolic.
Derivation
For the source finite-sum hard instance $g_i(x)$, define $f_i(x,y)=g_i(x)-(\mu_y/2)\|y\|_2^2$. This embedding preserves the smoothness bound, initial primal gap, and reduced objective, and makes the dual optimum zero for every $x$. One component joint-gradient query is simulated by one source query. The source result applies directly when $n\ge1024$. For $2\le n<1024$, set $k=\lceil1024/n\rceil$ and average the $kn$ source components in equal groups. Each target query costs $k\le512$ source queries, losing only a universal constant. Dimension may grow with the budget; queries, component selection, and unqueried outputs have no span restriction. If expected calls are at most $Q$, truncate at $\lceil6Q\rceil$ calls. The mean-square guarantee bounds the probability of error exceeding $\sqrt6\varepsilon$ by $1/6$. Adding timeout probability at most $1/6$ gives the source fixed-budget success guarantee. Retain the corresponding constant tightening of the source accuracy window.
Scope qualification
Explicit instance embedding from a lower bound for arbitrary randomized algorithms, without substituting a zero-respecting lower bound.
Branch condition
Assume $n\ge2$, $\kappa\ge1$, and $0<\varepsilon^2\le c_P\beta\Delta/6$, where $c_P>0$ is the universal accuracy constant in the finite-sum optimization lower bound. Take the worst case over all admissible finite dimensions. Universal constants may be tightened to absorb rounding; $2\le n<1024$ uses the stated equal-group averaging reduction.
Upper bound
\[O(n+\sqrt n\,a)\]
B8

Decoupling at condition number one and finite-sum variance reduction.

Near-Optimal Complexity of Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization ↗
Conditions
Every condition in the eight-axis specification and associated regime must hold jointly. Sufficient constants from different theorems are not assumed identical.
Algorithm scope
Upper bound from a specific randomized algorithm contained in the permitted class
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Constants
Use the source theorem’s universal constants except where derivative order or structural budgets are explicitly fixed. Unspecified sufficient thresholds remain symbolic.
Derivation
If $\kappa=1$, mean-square average smoothness, strong concavity of the average, and exact dual initialization imply $\Phi(x)=f(x,0)$. Only the average function must decouple. The source finite-sum variance-reduced method gives a fixed call cap $O(n+\sqrt n\,a)$ with randomized component sampling. Run directly at mean-square tolerance $\varepsilon$. The native guarantee is the target, and the fixed cap also bounds expected calls. No Markov conversion or truncation is needed.
Scope qualification
The recorded RPDA, SVRG, or decoupled finite-sum methods actually sample components randomly. Guarantee conversion does not remove this randomness.
Branch condition
$n\ge2$, $\kappa=1$, $\varepsilon>0$.
Gap or comparison
$O(1)$

Derivation
For a source finite-sum hard instance $g_i(x)$, define $f_i(x,y)=g_i(x)-(\mu_y/2)\|y\|_2^2$. The source result applies directly when $n\ge1024$. For $2\le n<1024$, let $k=\lceil1024/n\rceil$ and average the $kn$ source components in equal groups. Each target query uses $k\le512$ source calls, costing only a universal constant factor. Dimension may grow with the budget; queries, component choices, and unqueried outputs have no span restriction. Exact simulation preserves the fixed budget and instancewise success probability, yielding the $\Omega(n+\sqrt n\,a)$ lower bound without additional logarithmic loss.

Embedding an arbitrary-randomized finite-sum lower bound with an independent strongly concave quadratic term

Dense Weak Hiding: Closing Complexity Gaps in Nonconvex and PL Finite-Sum Optimization under Individual Smoothness ↗
Conditions
Every condition in the eight-axis specification and associated regime must hold jointly. Sufficient constants from different theorems are not assumed identical.
Algorithm scope
A lower bound for arbitrary randomized algorithms.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Constants
Use the source theorem’s universal constants except where derivative order or structural budgets are explicitly fixed. Unspecified sufficient thresholds remain symbolic.
Derivation
For the source finite-sum hard instance $g_i(x)$, define $f_i(x,y)=g_i(x)-(\mu_y/2)\|y\|_2^2$. This embedding preserves the smoothness bound, initial primal gap, and reduced objective, and makes the dual optimum zero for every $x$. One component joint-gradient query is simulated by one source query. The source result applies directly when $n\ge1024$. For $2\le n<1024$, set $k=\lceil1024/n\rceil$ and average the $kn$ source components in equal groups. Each target query costs $k\le512$ source queries, losing only a universal constant. Dimension may grow with the budget; queries, component selection, and unqueried outputs have no span restriction. If expected calls are at most $Q$, truncate at $\lceil6Q\rceil$ calls. The mean-square guarantee bounds the probability of error exceeding $\sqrt6\varepsilon$ by $1/6$. Adding timeout probability at most $1/6$ gives the source fixed-budget success guarantee. Retain the corresponding constant tightening of the source accuracy window.
Scope qualification
Explicit instance embedding from a lower bound for arbitrary randomized algorithms, without substituting a zero-respecting lower bound.
Branch condition
Assume $n\ge2$, $\kappa\ge1$, and $0<\varepsilon^2\le c_P\beta\Delta/6$, where $c_P>0$ is the universal accuracy constant in the finite-sum optimization lower bound. Take the worst case over all admissible finite dimensions. Universal constants may be tightened to absorb rounding; $2\le n<1024$ uses the stated equal-group averaging reduction.
Upper bound
\[O(\sqrt n\,\kappa a+n\ell_R)\]
B5

Randomized recursive proximal difference algorithm, RPDA

Near-Optimal Complexity of Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization ↗
Conditions
Every condition in the eight-axis specification and associated regime must hold jointly. Sufficient constants from different theorems are not assumed identical.
Algorithm scope
Upper bound from a specific randomized algorithm contained in the permitted class
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Constants
Use the source theorem’s universal constants except where derivative order or structural budgets are explicitly fixed. Unspecified sufficient thresholds remain symbolic.
Derivation
RPDA is a specific randomized witness, and its zero-respecting updates also belong to the larger allowed class. Each full gradient costs $n$ component calls, and a two-point component difference costs two calls. Counts include initialization, main iterations, and refinement; $\ell_R=1+\log(2+\kappa)+\log(2+(1+\kappa)^2a)$ records these logarithmic overheads. Run the source algorithm directly at mean-square tolerance $\varepsilon$. Its native guarantee is the target, and its fixed call cap also bounds expected calls. No Markov conversion or truncation is required.
Scope qualification
The recorded RPDA, SVRG, or decoupled finite-sum methods actually sample components randomly. Guarantee conversion does not remove this randomness.
Branch condition
$n\ge2$, $1\le\kappa\le\sqrt n$, $\varepsilon>0$.
Gap or comparison
$O\!\left(\frac{\sqrt n\,\kappa a+n\ell_R}{n+\sqrt n\,a}\right)$
Comparison argument
When n, $\kappa$, and a vary jointly, the envelope permits a polynomial gap $\kappa$. The gap may shrink if $\kappa$ is fixed or the n term dominates. If $\kappa\ge\kappa_0$, also take the maximum with the identical-component lower bound.

Constants

Derivation
Set all $n$ components equal to one exact-gradient NC-SC hard function. Average smoothness and exact dual initialization are preserved. Component indices reveal nothing, and each query equals one source joint-gradient call. The unrestricted randomized source lower bound gives $\Omega(\sqrt\kappa\,a)$ with its condition-number threshold and nontrivial accuracy window. To convert expected work and a mean-square guarantee to the source fixed budget, truncate at six times the expected budget and use source tolerance $\sqrt6\varepsilon$. The two failure probabilities are each at most $1/6$. Tighten the sufficient constant in the accuracy window accordingly.

Derivation
Divide every returned gradient by $\beta$ to simulate $\bar f=f/\beta$ without changing component-call counts. The normalized strong-concavity parameter is $1/\kappa$. For $\kappa\ge\sqrt n$, set regularization $1/\sqrt n$, obtaining work $O(n^{3/4}\sqrt\kappa(1+a)\log^2(2+\kappa))$ from the source formula. Full gradients and residual checks each cost $n$ component calls; $1+a$ retains at least one outer iteration. The source theorem directly controls $\mathbb E\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat x)\|_2^2$ and worst-instance expected work. Set its internal tolerance to $\varepsilon$ without converting it to a fixed-budget probability guarantee.

Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Constants

Derivation
For a source finite-sum hard instance $g_i(x)$, define $f_i(x,y)=g_i(x)-(\mu_y/2)\|y\|_2^2$. This preserves smoothness, the initial primal gap, and the reduced objective, and gives dual optimum zero for every $x$. One component joint-gradient query is simulated by one source query. The source result applies directly when $n\ge1024$. For $2\le n<1024$, let $k=\lceil1024/n\rceil$ and average the $kn$ source components in equal groups. Each target query uses $k\le512$ source calls, costing only a universal constant factor. Dimension may grow with the budget; queries, component choices, and unqueried outputs have no span restriction. Exact simulation preserves the fixed budget and instancewise success probability, yielding the $\Omega(n+\sqrt n\,a)$ lower bound without additional logarithmic loss.

Near-Optimal Complexity of Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization ↗
Conditions
Every condition in the eight-axis specification and associated regime must hold jointly. Sufficient constants from different theorems are not assumed identical.
Algorithm scope
Upper bound from a specific randomized algorithm contained in the permitted class
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Constants
Use the source theorem’s universal constants except where derivative order or structural budgets are explicitly fixed. Unspecified sufficient thresholds remain symbolic.
Derivation
RPDA is a specific randomized algorithm. Its updates are zero-respecting, so it also belongs to the larger algorithm class allowed here. A full gradient costs $n$ component calls; a two-point difference for the same component costs two calls. Counts include initialization, main iterations, and final refinement, and $\ell_R=1+\log(2+\kappa)+\log(2+(1+\kappa)^2a)$ records precisely these logarithmic overheads. Run the algorithm with internal mean-square tolerance $\eta=\varepsilon/\sqrt3$. Markov's inequality gives $\Pr(\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat x)\|_2>\varepsilon)\le\eta^2/\varepsilon^2=1/3$. The source algorithm already has a fixed call cap, so no runtime truncation is required.
Scope qualification
The recorded RPDA, SVRG, or decoupled finite-sum methods actually sample components randomly. Guarantee conversion does not remove this randomness.
Branch condition
$n\ge2$, $1\le\kappa\le\sqrt n$, $\varepsilon>0$.
Gap or comparison
$O\!\left(\frac{\sqrt n\,\kappa a+n\ell_R}{n+\sqrt n\,a}\right)$
Comparison argument
When n, $\kappa$, and a vary jointly, the envelope permits a polynomial gap $\kappa$. The gap may shrink if $\kappa$ is fixed or the n term dominates. If $\kappa\ge\kappa_0$, also take the maximum with the identical-component lower bound.

Sharp Fresh-Gradient Complexity of Nonconvex--Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization ↗
Conditions
Every condition in the eight-axis specification and associated regime must hold jointly. Sufficient constants from different theorems are not assumed identical.
Algorithm scope
A lower bound for arbitrary randomized algorithms.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Constants
Use the source theorem’s universal constants except where derivative order or structural budgets are explicitly fixed. Unspecified sufficient thresholds remain symbolic.
Derivation
Set all $n$ components equal to one exact-gradient NC-SC hard function. Average smoothness and exact dual initialization are unchanged, indices reveal nothing, and each query is one source joint-gradient call. The unrestricted randomized source lower bound yields $\Omega(\sqrt\kappa\,a)$ with its condition-number threshold and accuracy window. Simulation preserves the fixed call cap, output, and $2/3$ success probability; it uses no condition-number lower bound restricted to zero-respecting algorithms.
Scope qualification
Explicit instance embedding from a lower bound for arbitrary randomized algorithms, without substituting a zero-respecting lower bound.
Branch condition
Assume $n\ge2$, $\kappa\ge\kappa_0$, and $a\ge C_0$. The quantities $\kappa_0,C_0$ are the universal condition-number and accuracy thresholds in the exact-gradient nonconvex-strongly-concave lower bound. Take the worst case over all admissible finite dimensions and retain any tightening of universal constants needed to absorb rounding.
Upper bound
\[O\!\left(\min\{n^{3/4}\sqrt\kappa(1+a)\log^2(2+\kappa),(n+\kappa^2)(1+a+\ell_R)\}\right)\]
B13

Catalyst with gradient-based SVRG inner iterations.

Near-Optimal Complexity of Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization ↗The Complexity of Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization ↗
Conditions
Every condition in the eight-axis specification and associated regime must hold jointly. Sufficient constants from different theorems are not assumed identical.
Algorithm scope
Upper bound from a specific randomized algorithm contained in the permitted class
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Constants
Use the source theorem’s universal constants except where derivative order or structural budgets are explicitly fixed. Unspecified sufficient thresholds remain symbolic.
Derivation
Divide every returned gradient by $\beta$ to simulate $\bar f=f/\beta$ without changing component-query counts. The normalized strong-concavity parameter is $1/\kappa$. When $\kappa\ge\sqrt n$, choose regularization $1/\sqrt n$; the source bound gives work $O(n^{3/4}\sqrt\kappa(1+a)\log^2(2+\kappa))$. Charge $n$ component calls for every full gradient and residual check; $1+a$ ensures at least one outer iteration. Set internal mean-square tolerance $\eta=\varepsilon/\sqrt6$ and let $B(\eta)$ bound expected calls uniformly, including initialization and checks. Truncate at $N=\max\{1,\lceil6B(\eta)\rceil\}$ calls and return a fixed feasible point on timeout. By a union bound, error or timeout has probability at most $1/6+1/6=1/3$. No independence is needed, and only a constant factor is lost.
Scope qualification
The recorded RPDA, SVRG, or decoupled finite-sum methods actually sample components randomly. Guarantee conversion does not remove this randomness.
Branch condition
Require $n\ge2$, $\kappa\ge\sqrt n$, and $\varepsilon>0$. The expression retains $1+a$, so no additional nontrivial-accuracy threshold is imposed.
